## Cuernavaca — City of Eternal Spring!

This picturesque town has small houses, flower-filled balconies and narrow streets. The "eternal spring" of this colonial town brings sunny days and fairly cool nights.

## Cuernavaca — a Resort City!

Cuernavaca has long attracted the upper classes. Some of Mexico's wealthiest people have villas here; in earlier times, Aztec emperors built palaces in the area. Cuernavaca is known for its beautiful subtropical gardens, natural spas, historic haciendas and hidden ruins. The town also has museums, a cathedral and a 16th-century Franciscan monastery.

Kuravaina, also known as Kuraveina, is a tepui near Canaima. Its elevated areas offer views across the savanna, the forested Kuraupa Valley and neighboring table mountains. The contrast between open plains and flat-topped rock summits is especially striking here.

Exploring this tepui on foot complements boat routes around Canaima Lagoon. The walk and elevated views reveal the region's landscape from a different perspective. Kuravaina forms part of Canaima's natural surroundings, alongside better-known waterfalls and larger tepuis.

La Azulita lies in Mérida State, among the Venezuelan Andes. The settlement is surrounded by mountain slopes and linked by roads passing through cloud-forest areas. On a stop along an Andean route, its village buildings set against the green mountains are an attraction in themselves.

The settlement's Church of the Immaculate Conception stands out for its two towers. Travelers can also explore natural attractions nearby, including a local waterfall. La Azulita adds another dimension to a journey between lowland areas and highland settlements: a walk through the village offers a glimpse of daily life in a small mountain community.

## Arenal Volcano and the Waterfall: What to See in La Fortuna, Costa Rica

La Fortuna is situated 250 m above sea level, offering magnificent views of Arenal Volcano. The volcano's awakening in 1968 was triggered by a powerful earthquake, and a small village of around 100 residents was covered in lava.

Arenal Volcano stands 1,657 meters high and, together with the lake of the same name, forms the city's national park, known as "Arenal Volcano".

The volcano is continuously active and periodically produces small lava eruptions that pose no danger to people. The spectacular nature of this phenomenon makes the volcano popular with both tourists and local residents.
